denominator_notes: The 2306 checkpoints are repeated observations from 197 corridor-incident pairs and 178 publisher incident IDs; checkpoint counts are not independent event trials.

Incident model Switch-versus-own-Stay: 287 recommendations, 117 known outcomes (99 meaningful gains, 16 practical ties, 2 meaningful losses), 170 unknown. Do not report 99/117 as all-recommendation success or as incremental benefit over raw MTA.
Raw-MTA Stay/model Switch: 58 decisions, 22 known comparisons (13 gains, 9 ties), 36 unknown. Primary representatives: 7 decisions, 2 known comparisons (1 gain, 1 tie), 5 unknown.

Actual incident-policy versus raw-policy recommendations: 992 action-eligible checkpoints, 641 known paired outcomes (56 gains, 574 ties, 11 losses), 351 unknown. The denominator differs from model-Switch-versus-own-Stay.

Severe exposure: 183 checkpoints from 12 corridor incidents and 11 publishers; 34 model Switch recommendations contain 10 gains, 1 tie, 23 unknown. Only one primary earliest-weekday representative is severe, because later severity escalation remains in checkpoint strata.
Planned closure timing is separately frozen: 12 active checkpoints and one primary representative. Their coexistence with unplanned notices does not establish unplanned causation.
November 2–15 overlaps prior project exploration. November 16–18 is separately reported and the entire November view is not a pristine untouched final test.
This audit verifies arithmetic, strict action recomputation and stored screened MTA-proxy outcome use; it does not independently establish physical train arrivals or reconstruct endpoint labels.
